title: Drummers, trombonists and bassists
summary: Short opinions on Rufus Jones, Booty Wood, Jimmy Blanton and Gus Johnson.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Well, listen, now, let's talk about drummers just for a moment. What about Rufus in that band?
Well, that wasn't the kind of drummer you looked to hear in that band, was it?
Yeah, he was all right. He was a good drummer.
He's a good drummer, isn't he? Yeah. Okay. Yeah, well, what about Bootie Wood and Britt Woodman. What about those trombone players?
Oh, Bootie Wood's a fine trombone player.
No. Bootie played more with the plunger than anybody else got to play after -- almost after Tricky, wouldn't you say?
Yeah. Well, Quentin Jackson used it.
He was a very good player.
He was a good musician, wasn't he?

Well, I was going to ask you about some of those bass players. I was going to ask you about Pettiford and about Ernie Shepherd. But really, you sort of intimated that it was more a question of soloists, wasn't it?
I enjoyed Blanton's solo work very much.
But I think the band was a little too heavy for Blanton. You know, as a bass player.
Yeah. Because he was young, too, wasn't he?
I told you the one I liked was Billy Taylor.
I just want to ask you about Gus Johnson,
because I saw you had him working for you at one time. You like him as a drummer?

Yeah. Gus Johnson's a very fine drummer. According to what type you wanted him for. Gus Johnson is drumming now for singers in small groups. It's a different feeling with small groups and singers, and you fitting in with a big band.
With a big band, yeah. But he -- I mean he was a heavy enough drummer to fit in with a band. Well, that's how he started off, as a band drummer, didn't he?
